text:
ryan_customer: Hey support — since yesterday ~10:30 UTC our uploads are intermittently routed to EU and we’re seeing +200ms latency and EU billing for some requests. We definitely set X-Client-Region: us-west and also pass ?region=us-west on the upload POST. Can reproduce.

ryan_customer: Repro with curl below (I attached a small sample):

```bash
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads?region=us-west' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  --data-binary @small-file.bin
```

ryan_customer: Response from our logs (initial request):

```
HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
Location: https://api-uploads.eu.redwood.ai/v1/uploads?region=us-west
Content-Length: 0
```

ryan_customer: Follow-up request (client followed redirect) in our server logs shows no X-Client-Region header — router picked eu edge based on host and billed eu. Using curl -L or axios/fetch behaves the same: custom headers are dropped on cross-host redirect.

olivia_support: Thanks @ryan_customer — can you confirm SDK/client version? Also paste the raw request headers for both initial and follow-up if possible.

ryan_customer: We're on our own tiny wrapper around axios 1.5.2. Paste of headers (sanitized):

Initial:
```
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Client-Region: us-west
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
```

Follow-up (to api-uploads.eu...):
```
Host: api-uploads.eu.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
# no X-Client-Region
```

kai_sdk: this is a known cross-host redirect issue — most HTTP clients do NOT forward custom headers when following redirects to a different origin. Our uploads flow relies on the client header to select edge during the second hop, which is brittle if we respond with a 307 to a different host. We added the 307 so uploads stream from a region-specific upload domain, but didn't account for header-loss on redirect.

sre_oncall: Short-term mitigations: 1) Instruct customers to turn off automatic redirect-following and retry the Location with the same headers (ugly), or 2) have the redirect target include region in the host itself (eg: us-west.api-uploads.redwood.ai) so the client follows directly to the correct edge without needing X-Client-Region. Also consider treating query param region as authoritative when header missing on follow-up.

kai_sdk: Agreed — we should update SDK docs to call out that clients must preserve region info across redirects, but that's not reliable for third-party clients. Server-side change is better.

tile_engineer: Filed RUN-1234: "upload redirect must preserve region routing when header absent". Proposed plan:
- Bake region into redirect host (us-west/api-uploads) to avoid reliance on custom header.
- Router change: if follow-up request arrives without X-Client-Region but has ?region=... in Location or original request, use that query param during final routing.
- Ensure metrics attribution uses initial request's region tag.
Canary: 48h starting tomorrow 09:00 UTC, then gradual rollout.

olivia_support: @billing_bot tagging for potential backbilling exposure for customers affected. Ryan — we'll keep billing in the loop.

billing_bot: Forwarded to billing queue (priority: medium).

ryan_customer: Thanks — can you confirm expected ETA for canary/start? The extra egress/billing is noticeable for a small % of requests.

tile_engineer: Canary starts 09:00 UTC tomorrow, monitoring dashboards set up (latency + region labels). We'll post live update in this thread once canary starts and after 24h. :thumbsup:

olivia_support: Closing loop for now — assigning to RUN-1234 and leaving thread pinned to the ticket. Please paste any additional repro logs here if you see regression during canary.

ryan_customer: Will do, thanks everyone.
